minutes.headline: Board voted to join the regional stormwater coalition and agreed to let the Boys and Girls Club use a town lot.
minutes.summary: The Select Board heard a Hall of Fame request for a home for trophy cases and voted to join the Central Mass regional stormwater coalition. It ratified two appointments, then discussed a letter and an extension request over the enforcement order on town land at Pleasant Street. It also debated afternoon use of the town parking lot by the Boys and Girls Club, and heard about insurance rewards credits and health insurance data.

public_comment.topic: Hall of Fame committee asked for a permanent or temporary home for its trophy cases at the TCP building before the high school closes.
Described the display cases, plaque counts and future inductions.
Urged the board to press the property owner at 101 Pleasant Street, check his equipment license, and send an official to the Conservation Commission.
Asked about more handicap parking, two-hour signs, Teen Center gym access, backed the ZBA appointment, and asked about pay-as-you-throw bag penalties and heavier bags.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to enter the inter-municipal agreement joining the Central Mass regional stormwater coalition.
The board agreed to give the Boys and Girls Club exclusive afternoon use of the town lot on weekdays, if on-street employee parking is eliminated and signs are posted.
The board decided to send letters to the alleged violator and to Conservation asking for an extension of the enforcement order on town land at Pleasant Street.
The board ratified a DPW heavy equipment operator appointment, appointed a ZBA member to June 30, 2017, and passed the Memorial Day flag resolution.
The pay-as-you-throw bag item was continued to the next meeting, and the hazard mitigation plan was set for board action in June.

why_it_matters: Joining the stormwater coalition ties the town to a shared regional arrangement for stormwater compliance, which can shape future public works costs paid from the town budget, mostly taxes.

The parking lot decision changes who can use a town lot on weekday afternoons and removes on-street employee parking, and the pay-as-you-throw bag rules that may affect household trash costs are still undecided.
watch_next: The pay-as-you-throw bag item returns at the next Select Board meeting.
The hazard mitigation plan is scheduled for board action in June.
